_note: Confirmed 1 Nov 2026 from the pcaps (src/diag/find_attackers.py, src/diag/inspect_internal.py, src/diag/check_http.sh, src/diag/check_bruteforce_split.py, src/diag/quick_talkers.sh, src/diag/attacker_ports.sh, src/diag/run_quick_talkers.sh). IP rule: one end is an attacker, the other a victim (listed victims, else any LAN host except .1/.255), on victim_ports when listed. MAC rule (ARP spoofing): first packet from/to the attacker MAC, attacker's own IP not an endpoint. Large files: attackers first found in the first 300,000 packets; flood sources were then re-counted over the whole trimmed file (1M packets) with src/diag/victim_sources.sh.

Recon-PortScan.evidence: 119k flows to 58 hosts, 1,001 distinct dst ports

SqlInjection.evidence: 350 HTTP requests to /dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ with SLEEP/UNION payloads on .4, .86, .217

XSS.evidence: HTTP requests to /dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_d|xss_r/ with <script> payloads on .11, .13, .236

DictionaryBruteForce.evidence: SSH brute force on .67:22 (13:21-13:43), then RTSP on .11:554 and .140:554 (13:43-15:01); .65's Chromecast (8009) and ICMP flows are not part of the attack

DDoS-SYN_Flood.evidence: src/diag/victim_sources.sh on the trimmed file (1M packets): exactly six sources send to .245:4070 (.201 448,598; .99 154,149; .36 136,690; .34 89,551; .153 76,908; .87 72,324). .36 joins after the first 300,000 packets and was first missed (found by src/diag/diagnose_errors.py: 65,525 'Benign' flows .36 -> .245:4070 predicted DDoS-SYN)

DoS-HTTP_Flood.evidence: .66 -> .71 161,051 and -> .141 16,577 of the first 300,000 packets; 99,895 of .66's first 100,000 packets go to port 80

Mirai-udpplain.evidence: seven sources send 298,838 of the first 300,000 packets to .191 (UDP, random ports)

MITM-ArpSpoofing.evidence: dc:a6:32:dc:27:d5 (Raspberry Pi OUI) sends ARP replies claiming both 192.168.137.1 (router, real MAC 3c:18:a0:41:c3:a0) and its own .65
